subject: Collins Center Presentation on Executive Government Models
overview: The Charter Study Committee discussed prioritization of charter review topics and received an overview from the Collins Center comparing executive models of municipal government. The committee also scheduled its first public information session for June 8, 2023, and reviewed public outreach strategies and budget allocations.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the committee's March meeting.

items.title: Discussion on Charter Study Priorities
items.summary: Members shared initial priorities for charter review, focusing on the roles of the mayor, city council representation, school committee governance under general law, and the necessity of engaging community members alongside elected officials.

items.title: Collins Center Presentation on Executive Government Models
items.summary: Collins Center representatives presented the structures, tradeoffs, and legal frameworks of weak mayor, strong mayor, and council-manager forms of municipal government, followed by committee discussion on appointment powers and school committee relationships.

items.title: Public Engagement Planning
items.summary: The committee scheduled a hybrid public information session for June 8 at City Hall from 7:00 to 8:30 PM, approved translating outreach flyers into five languages for $250, and discussed tabling at community events and distributing flyers throughout the city.

items.title: Budget Update
items.summary: The committee reported an initial municipal budget allocation of $2,500, intended primarily to cover document translation and survey expenses through 2023.

items.title: Meeting Schedule and Format
items.summary: The committee decided to maintain its monthly schedule on the first Thursday of the month, with plans to explore forming subcommittees to handle specialized work between meetings.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: During public comment, a resident discussed the practice of requiring addresses from speakers and the accessibility of committee materials and contact information on the city website.
